**Old Navy** is an American clothing and accessories retailing company owned by [Gap Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gap_Inc. "Gap Inc."), a [multinational corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Navy#cite_note-3) It has corporate operations in the [Mission Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_Bay,_San_Francisco "Mission Bay, San Francisco") neighborhood of [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), California. The largest of the Old Navy stores are its flagship stores, located in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), [Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila "Manila"), and [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City").

**Kate Spade New York** (stylized as "kate spade NEW YORK" sometimes with a "♠") is an American fashion house founded in January 1993 by [Kate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade "Kate Spade") and [Andy Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade "Andy Spade"), along with [Elyce Arons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elyce_Arons "Elyce Arons") and Pamela Bell. In 2017, the company was purchased by [Tapestry, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapestry,_Inc. "Tapestry, Inc."), formerly known as [Coach, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coach_New_York "Coach New York")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-2)
[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/Kate_spade_new_york_-C88F8F.jpg/250px-Kate_spade_new_york_-C88F8F.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kate_spade_new_york_-C88F8F.jpg)

Temporary shop in New York

### Prior to company creation
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kate_Spade_New_York&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Prior to company creation")]
Katherine Noel Brosnahan (later known as [Kate Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade "Kate Spade")) was born on December 24, 1962, in [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"). She grew up in Kansas City and went to an all-girls Catholic high school. Eventually she moved to Arizona, where she attended [Arizona State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_State_University "Arizona State University") and graduated in 1985.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-:0-3) It is there that she met her future husband, [Andy Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade "Andy Spade"). Katherine majored in journalism, while Andy majored in architecture.
In 1986, after completing their education, the couple moved to [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-4) It was in New York that Katherine worked as a style editor for _[Mademoiselle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mademoiselle\_(magazine) "Mademoiselle (magazine)")_, but left in 1991 (with the title of senior editor/head of accessories) to start her own [handbag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handbag "Handbag") line.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-5) To get inspiration, Kate browsed local [flea markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flea_market "Flea market") and secondhand stores. She also researched the styles, fabrics, and potential production costs of making her own handbags. The team slowly worked their way up the social ladder until they were able to create a company that would be noticed by the public.

### Prior to company creation
Kate Spade New York was founded in 1993 by Katherine Noel Brosnahan and her husband/business partner Andy Spade, along with Elyce Arons and Pamela Bell.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-6) Kate Spade New York started after a suggestion from Andy when Katherine was unsure about her next career move after working six years at _Mademoiselle_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-7) Originally, the business started out with the Sam handbag.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-:0-3) Eventually, Andy withdrew $35,000 from his [401K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/401K "401K") account to fund the production of Katherine's handbags. Her debut line infused classic shapes, colors, and fabrics into a now iconic[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] square bag with a small black label sewn to the outside of the bag that said "Kate Spade New York." Her main [target market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_market "Target market") at this time was the [upper middle class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_middle_class "Upper middle class").
In 1996, Spade's company opened its first shop in New York City's [SoHo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoHo "SoHo") neighborhood. Kate Spade rose in eight months after a journalist at Cleveland Research Co. recommended buying the shares because of the brand's growth potential.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-:1-8)

### Prior to company creation
After 1998 the company began to expand, with sales totaling $27 million. In 1999, [Neiman Marcus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neiman_Marcus "Neiman Marcus") Group paid $34 million for a 56% stake of the company.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-9) In 2006 when Neiman Marcus Group acquired the remaining 44% stake in Kate Spade for $59.4 M, revenue was reportedly near $99 million.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-10) This acquisition valued the company at $134 million.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-11)
In 2004, Kate Spade operated only 13 stores in the United States, and did not [ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship "Ship") out of the country (Cohen 198). The company initially sold handbags, but eventually extended to include stationery, personal organizers, address books, shoes, beauty products, perfume, raincoats, pajamas, eyewear, and clothing. It now has a full women's clothing line. The business' clothing and handbag lines are featured in retail stores all across the United States. Products are easily and continuously shipped around the world. By 2004, Kate Spade & Co. was worth $70 million, not including the complementary company Jack Spade.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-12) Kate Spade has over 180 stores around the world, and is sold in more than 400 stores worldwide (Cohen 198). Kate and Andy went from taking "the nothing black bag" to a creative personalized purse, to later creating merchandise from the simple tote to home decor and bedding.

Spade was born Katherine Noel Brosnahan on December 24, 1962, in [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), the daughter of June (née Mullen) and Francis (Frank) Brosnahan,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-IrishCentral-3) who owned a road-construction company.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-NYT_1999_article-4) She was of mostly Irish descent.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-IrishCentral-3) After graduating from [St. Teresa's Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Teresa's_Academy "St. Teresa's Academy"), an all-female Catholic high school, Spade attended the [University of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kansas "University of Kansas"). She later transferred to [Arizona State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_State_University "Arizona State University"). She joined the [Kappa Kappa Gamma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kappa_Kappa_Gamma "Kappa Kappa Gamma") sorority and graduated with a journalism degree in 1985, thinking she would go into television production. While in college, she worked in sales at Carter's Men Shop, a men's clothing store in [Phoenix, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona "Phoenix, Arizona"). One co-worker there was [Andy Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade "Andy Spade"), who later became her husband and business partner.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-NYT_1999_article-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-6)

By 1986, the couple had moved to [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"). Kate worked in the accessories department at _[Mademoiselle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mademoiselle\_(magazine) "Mademoiselle (magazine)")_. She left _Mademoiselle_ in 1991, achieving the rank of senior [fashion editor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_editor "Fashion editor") and head of accessories.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-NYT_obituary-7) While working for _Mademoiselle_, she had noticed that the market lacked stylish, affordable, and sensible handbags, so decided to create her own.

### Kate Spade New York
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kate_Spade&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Kate Spade New York")]
[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Kate-spade-logo.jpg/250px-Kate-spade-logo.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kate-spade-logo.jpg)
Kate Spade logo
[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Kate_Spade_handbag.jpg/250px-Kate_Spade_handbag.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kate_Spade_handbag.jpg)
A Kate Spade handbag
Kate and Andy co-founded Kate Spade New York, along with Elyce Arons and Pamela Bell, in January 1993.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-biographysite-8) Spade was initially undecided on the brand's name, because Andy and she had not yet married, and "Kate Brosnahan" seemed a cumbersome name for a fashion label. She considered a number of names, but agreed when Andy suggested "Kate Spade", as she would take the name Spade after their marriage.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-9)

## Early life and education
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andy_Spade&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]
Spade was born in Michigan, the middle child in a family of three brothers. His younger brother is actor and comedian [David Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Spade "David Spade").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-old-school_cool-2) The family moved to Arizona when Andy was six. He attended [Arizona State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_State_University "Arizona State University"), where he met his future wife. During college, he and a friend founded the advertising firm Spade & Hannawell, which was named one of Arizona's Top 10 New Companies in 1987.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-Power_Couple-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-Giant_in_New_York-4)
Spade started his career in advertising, working on brands including [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola"), [Lexus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexus "Lexus"), and [Paul Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Stuart "Paul Stuart").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-5) He left his job in 1996 to work full-time on the business he and his wife had started.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-How_We_Bagged-6)

## Early life and education
In 1993, he and his wife founded the fashion and lifestyle brand [Kate Spade New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York "Kate Spade New York"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-7) and in 1999, the men's brand [Jack Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Spade "Jack Spade").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-Mixed_Bag-8)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-Power_Couple-3)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-How_We_Bagged-6)
In 2013, he launched a collection of loungewear, [Sleepy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleepy_Jones "Sleepy Jones"), with Anthony Sperduti and Chad Buri.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-9)

## Early life and education
In 2008, Spade and Sperduti established [Partners & Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partners_&_Spade "Partners & Spade"), a creative branding studio and storefront in the NoHo neighborhood of Manhattan. He also produced director [Josh Safdie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Safdie "Josh Safdie")'s debut feature film, [The Pleasure of Being Robbed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pleasure_of_Being_Robbed "The Pleasure of Being Robbed") (2008),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-10) and has conceived and published several photography and concept books through such imprints as A.S. Books,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-11) Jack Spade Press,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-12) and Kate Spade Editions,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-13) as well as independently.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-14)
Spade was married to designer [Kate Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade "Kate Spade") (née Brosnahan) from 1994 until her death on June 5, 2018.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-15) They had one daughter, born in February 2005.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-16) Actress [Rachel Brosnahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Brosnahan "Rachel Brosnahan") is Spade's niece.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-17)

### Prior to company creation
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kate_Spade_New_York&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Prior to company creation")]
Katherine Noel Brosnahan (later known as [Kate Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade "Kate Spade")) was born on December 24, 1962, in [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"). She grew up in Kansas City and went to an all-girls Catholic high school. Eventually she moved to Arizona, where she attended [Arizona State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_State_University "Arizona State University") and graduated in 1985.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-:0-3) It is there that she met her future husband, [Andy Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade "Andy Spade"). Katherine majored in journalism, while Andy majored in architecture.
In 1986, after completing their education, the couple moved to [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-4) It was in New York that Katherine worked as a style editor for _[Mademoiselle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mademoiselle\_(magazine) "Mademoiselle (magazine)")_, but left in 1991 (with the title of senior editor/head of accessories) to start her own [handbag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handbag "Handbag") line.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-5) To get inspiration, Kate browsed local [flea markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flea_market "Flea market") and secondhand stores. She also researched the styles, fabrics, and potential production costs of making her own handbags. The team slowly worked their way up the social ladder until they were able to create a company that would be noticed by the public.

### Prior to company creation
Kate Spade New York was founded in 1993 by Katherine Noel Brosnahan and her husband/business partner Andy Spade, along with Elyce Arons and Pamela Bell.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-6) Kate Spade New York started after a suggestion from Andy when Katherine was unsure about her next career move after working six years at _Mademoiselle_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-7) Originally, the business started out with the Sam handbag.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-:0-3) Eventually, Andy withdrew $35,000 from his [401K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/401K "401K") account to fund the production of Katherine's handbags. Her debut line infused classic shapes, colors, and fabrics into a now iconic[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] square bag with a small black label sewn to the outside of the bag that said "Kate Spade New York." Her main [target market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_market "Target market") at this time was the [upper middle class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_middle_class "Upper middle class").
In 1996, Spade's company opened its first shop in New York City's [SoHo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoHo "SoHo") neighborhood. Kate Spade rose in eight months after a journalist at Cleveland Research Co. recommended buying the shares because of the brand's growth potential.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-:1-8)
texts.5:
### Prior to company creation
After 1998 the company began to expand, with sales totaling $27 million. In 1999, [Neiman Marcus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neiman_Marcus "Neiman Marcus") Group paid $34 million for a 56% stake of the company.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-9) In 2006 when Neiman Marcus Group acquired the remaining 44% stake in Kate Spade for $59.4 M, revenue was reportedly near $99 million.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-10) This acquisition valued the company at $134 million.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-11)
In 2004, Kate Spade operated only 13 stores in the United States, and did not [ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship "Ship") out of the country (Cohen 198). The company initially sold handbags, but eventually extended to include stationery, personal organizers, address books, shoes, beauty products, perfume, raincoats, pajamas, eyewear, and clothing. It now has a full women's clothing line. The business' clothing and handbag lines are featured in retail stores all across the United States. Products are easily and continuously shipped around the world. By 2004, Kate Spade & Co. was worth $70 million, not including the complementary company Jack Spade.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York#cite_note-12) Kate Spade has over 180 stores around the world, and is sold in more than 400 stores worldwide (Cohen 198). Kate and Andy went from taking "the nothing black bag" to a creative personalized purse, to later creating merchandise from the simple tote to home decor and bedding.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andy_Spade&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]
Spade was born in Michigan, the middle child in a family of three brothers. His younger brother is actor and comedian [David Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Spade "David Spade").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-old-school_cool-2) The family moved to Arizona when Andy was six. He attended [Arizona State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_State_University "Arizona State University"), where he met his future wife. During college, he and a friend founded the advertising firm Spade & Hannawell, which was named one of Arizona's Top 10 New Companies in 1987.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-Power_Couple-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-Giant_in_New_York-4)
Spade started his career in advertising, working on brands including [Coca-Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coca-Cola "Coca-Cola"), [Lexus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexus "Lexus"), and [Paul Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Stuart "Paul Stuart").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-5) He left his job in 1996 to work full-time on the business he and his wife had started.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-How_We_Bagged-6)

## Early life and education
In 1993, he and his wife founded the fashion and lifestyle brand [Kate Spade New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade_New_York "Kate Spade New York"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-7) and in 1999, the men's brand [Jack Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Spade "Jack Spade").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-Mixed_Bag-8)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-Power_Couple-3)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-How_We_Bagged-6)
In 2013, he launched a collection of loungewear, [Sleepy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleepy_Jones "Sleepy Jones"), with Anthony Sperduti and Chad Buri.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-9)

In 2008, Spade and Sperduti established [Partners & Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partners_&_Spade "Partners & Spade"), a creative branding studio and storefront in the NoHo neighborhood of Manhattan. Spade was married to designer [Kate Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade "Kate Spade") (née Brosnahan) from 1994 until her death on June 5, 2018.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-15) They had one daughter, born in February 2005.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-16) Actress [Rachel Brosnahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Brosnahan "Rachel Brosnahan") is Spade's niece.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade#cite_note-17)

texts.2: Spade was born Katherine Noel Brosnahan on December 24, 1962, in [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), the daughter of June (née Mullen) and Francis (Frank) Brosnahan,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-IrishCentral-3) who owned a road-construction company.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-NYT_1999_article-4) She was of mostly Irish descent.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-IrishCentral-3) After graduating from [St. Teresa's Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Teresa's_Academy "St. Teresa's Academy"), an all-female Catholic high school, Spade attended the [University of Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kansas "University of Kansas"). She later transferred to [Arizona State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_State_University "Arizona State University"). She joined the [Kappa Kappa Gamma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kappa_Kappa_Gamma "Kappa Kappa Gamma") sorority and graduated with a journalism degree in 1985, thinking she would go into television production. While in college, she worked in sales at Carter's Men Shop, a men's clothing store in [Phoenix, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix,_Arizona "Phoenix, Arizona"). One co-worker there was [Andy Spade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Spade "Andy Spade"), who later became her husband and business partner.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-NYT_1999_article-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-6)
texts.3: By 1986, the couple had moved to [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"). Kate worked in the accessories department at _[Mademoiselle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mademoiselle\_(magazine) "Mademoiselle (magazine)")_. She left _Mademoiselle_ in 1991, achieving the rank of senior [fashion editor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion_editor "Fashion editor") and head of accessories.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Spade#cite_note-NYT_obituary-7) While working for _Mademoiselle_, she had noticed that the market lacked stylish, affordable, and sensible handbags, so decided to create her own.

**Hi. My name is Burnie. Or Alex Burnard.Or both.**
I’m a longtime veteran of Crispin Porter + Bogusky where I spent over fifteen years rising through the ranks - joining as an Art Director in 1998 to Executive Creative Director of the Miami office in 2011. My last role there was that of Chief Innovation Officer for the network of offices.
During my time at CP+B, the agency was named Agency of the Year nine times and was recognized as the Worldwide Agency of the Decade in 2010.
I love creating strategic based, creative platforms for brands that allow clients to find their place in pop culture. I’ve been lucky enough to do that for a number of iconic brands such as: Coke Zero, Ikea, Maxim, Nike, Under Armour, Truth, Molson, Vitamin Water, Buell Motorcycles, Burger King, AND1, Shimano, Pilar Rum and GT Bicycles.
**Some of the highlights of my time at CP+B:**
- The North American launch of Coke Zero. My partner and I then proceeding to steward the brand for it’s first seven years. The result is the creation of the most successful new product launch for the Coca-Cola company since Diet Coke.

- An integral part of defining the Truth brand which resulted in the most effective anti-tobacco campaign in history. (It was estimated at one point to have saved over 200,000 lives)It was also named by Ad Age as one of the top 20 campaigns of this century.

Thanks.

## 1996 STEPHON MARBURY
In 1996, legendary NBA player and future Hall of Famer Stephon Marbury became AND1’s first NBA ambassador, paving the way for the scores of players the brand would sign in the years to come. Marbury was named to the All-Rookie Team in’97 and went on to lead the Timberwolves to the NBA Playoffs in ‘97 and’98, bringing AND1 much fame in its early stages.
With the Marbury signing, AND1 launched its first pair of basketball sneakers, essentially expanding the brand into the footwear category. The brand debuted its footwear at the 1997 NBA All-Star Game, officially releasing the Stephon Marburys, which wound up becoming one of AND1’s greatest shoes.
![Image 4](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/mixtapes-04.png?v=1784544809&width=1000)

## 1998 THE SKIP TAPE
In late 1998, a videotape containing streetball stunts was delivered to AND1 by a high school coach in New York. The low-quality video was a “mixtape” of hip-hop music and dazzling basketball moves by a streetballer named Rafer Alston, who had just entered the 1998 NBA Draft.
A short while later, AND1 edited and reprinted 50,000 digital copies of Alston’s Mixtape and distributed them across America through basketball camps, clinics and record labels. The tape instantly became the buzz of the basketball world.
The videotape was later known as the "Skip Tape," referring to Alston's streetball nickname "Skip 2 My Lou." Alston, although not yet in the NBA, would soon sign with AND1.
![Image 5](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/mixtapes-05.png?v=1784544901&width=1000)

## 1999 THE MIXTAPE
Once the “Skip Tape” created major buzz for AND1, the brand began to produce multiple “AND1 Mixtapes." [The Mixtapes](https://and1.com/pages/mixtape-legends "Mixtape Legends") were all similar to the Skip Tape - clips of highly entertaining streetball moves with hip-hop and rap playing in the background.
The Mixtape would soon become a major selling tool with the Sports Specialty Retailers. AND1 partnered with FootAction in the summer of ‘99 to start distributing the mixtape nationally, with FootAction offering a free Mixtape DVD with the purchase of any sneakers or apparel. Demand for the tapes reached an unprecedented level as approximately 200,000 tapes were distributed in the span of three weeks, making the Mixtape one of the most successful promotions in US retail history.
The Mixtape’s success resulted in AND1 touring the country every summer in search of the next streetball legends to appear on subsequent Mixtapes.
![Image 6](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/Picture6.jpg?v=1784545028&width=922)

## 2000 THE DUNK CONTEST
The AND1 Tai Chis were always one of the brand’s greatest shoes, known for both performance and style with a yin yang look. But in 2000, they were instantly vaulted into the stratosphere. At the time Vince Carter was between contracts, so he decided to give the Tai Chis a go. Carter then put on one of the greatest performances in NBA Dunk Contest history—all while wearing the red and white Tai Chis.
In the words of Ryan Drew, former VP of footwear at AND1: “Not only was that maybe the best series of dunks I have ever seen, because it was just dunks that you’d never even seen before, but it was almost like the dunks that he had done were tailor made for the color-blocking of the shoe. The dunk where he goes between the legs, he’s got one leg up and the ball is under, and you see one half red and one half white. It was unbelievable. Then, every single image for the next three or four months that was NBA related was him in the Dunk Contest with our shoe on.”
![Image 7](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/marbury2-07.png?v=1784545250&width=1000)

## 2001 NBA AMBASSADORS
Beginning with the Marbury signing and the Rafer Alston discovery two years later, NBA players throughout the league began to sign with AND1, siding with the "underdog" in a major power play competing with the bigger brands. By the 2001 season, AND1 was second in market share among NBA endorsees, just eight years after its inception.
Players like Latrell Sprewell, Kevin Garnett and Jamal Crawford brought AND1 into the national spotlight. The players AND1 signed always matched the brand’s streetball profile, with the in-your-face, best-on-court attitude.
![Image 8](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/mixtape_bus-08.png?v=1784545452&width=1000)

**AND1** is an American footwear and clothing company specializing in [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") shoes, clothing, and sporting goods. AND1 was founded on August 13, 1993. The company focuses strictly on basketball and is a subsidiary of Galaxy Universal.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-galax-1)
The company sponsors [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA "NBA") athletes, as well as numerous high school and AAU teams in the United States.

In 1993, AND1 began as a graduate school project [partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partnership "Partnership") of Jay Coen Gilbert, Seth Berger, and Tom Austin while they were graduate students at the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania")'s [Wharton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School "Wharton School").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:042-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:1-3) The company name is derived from a phrase used by [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball")[broadcasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_presenter "Sports presenter") to denote a [free throw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_throw "Free throw") awarded to a player against whom a foul has been committed while scoring a goal.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:44-4)

The brand started by selling T-shirts out of the back of a car.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:32-5) Early advertising strategies included other basketball [slogans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slogans "Slogans") and [trash talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trash_talk "Trash talk"), such as "Pass. Save Yourself The Embarrassment".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-chicago-sports-review3-6) They targeted the niche market of street basketball players and avoided branching out to other markets.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-7)[Foot Locker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot_Locker "Foot Locker") began to sell the shirts, and within the second year of launching, the business reached 1,500 stores across America.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:042-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:1-3) The company's first big endorsee was [Larry Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Johnson_(basketball,_born_1969) "Larry Johnson (basketball, born 1969)"), who briefly wore their shirts.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:44-4)

### The Skip Tape and success
In 1999 at [Haverford College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haverford_College "Haverford College") in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), AND1 shot its first series of [commercials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercials "Commercials") and [print ads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Print_ad "Print ad")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:042-2) incorporating [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA "NBA") players [Darrell Armstrong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darrell_Armstrong "Darrell Armstrong"), [Rex Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Chapman "Rex Chapman"), Ab Osondu, [Raef LaFrentz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raef_LaFrentz "Raef LaFrentz"), [Toby Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toby_Bailey "Toby Bailey"), and [Miles Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miles_Simon "Miles Simon").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:542-11) The company signed [Latrell Sprewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latrell_Sprewell "Latrell Sprewell") in 1999.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:32-5) His shoe, the AND1 Spree, was released in 2002.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-15) When the traditional marketing campaign proved unsuccessful, a strategy was formed to use the Skip tape. It was edited and reprinted into 50,000 copies, and over the next eight weeks, distributed across basketball camps, clinics, and record labels.

### The Skip Tape and success
The tape would become the first "[Mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_mixtape "Video mixtape")", and quickly made Alston into a celebrity.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:542-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:222-13)
When AND1 became a product partner with [FootAction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot_Locker "Foot Locker"), this strategy evolved into a national program.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:44-4)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:542-11) Starting in the summer of 1999, a free AND1 Mixtape was given with any purchase. Approximately 200,000 tapes were distributed in the span of three weeks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-chicago-sports-review3-6)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:222-13)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:62-16) It proved to be so successful that the company put together a team of streetball legends to serve as a traveling team and filmed new mixtapes.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:542-11) By the end of the year, the Philadelphia-based company had more than 70 employees.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:44-4)
[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/And1_basketball_shoes.jpg/250px-And1_basketball_shoes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:And1_basketball_shoes.jpg)
AND1 basketball shoes

### The Skip Tape and success
AND1 gained fame when [Vince Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Carter "Vince Carter") won the 2000 [Slam Dunk Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slam_Dunk_Contest "Slam Dunk Contest") while wearing its Tai Chi shoes.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-Souphanh-9)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-17) He was then featured on the cover of the April 2000 issue of [Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slam_(magazine) "Slam (magazine)") wearing another pair.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-18) The company went on to sell more than a million shoes.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-19) By the 2001 season, AND1 was second only to Nike in market share and had $285 million in revenue.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:042-2) The company also signed [Kevin Garnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Garnett "Kevin Garnett") and [Jamal Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamal_Crawford "Jamal Crawford").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-21)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:1-3)

### The Skip Tape and success
In 2002, the AND1 summer tours were expanded into the Mixtape Tour. "Open runs" were also introduced, where local street ballers were given a chance to go up against AND1's team. The best from that group would join the summer tour and receive endorsement deals from AND1. [Grayson Boucher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grayson_Boucher "Grayson Boucher"), aka "The Professor," was the first to win a spot on the team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-chicago-sports-review3-6)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:542-11)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:2-22) Founder Tom Austin left the company in 2003.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:042-2) Another iconic moment for the brand came in 2004, when [Chauncey Billups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauncey_Billups "Chauncey Billups") won the [NBA Finals MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player "NBA Finals Most Valuable Player") while wearing the AND1 Rise sneaker.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-23)

AND1 **began its journey in 1993** when Jay Coen Gilbert, Seth Berger, and Tom Austin started a t-shirt company out of the trunk of a car **while studying at the University of Pennsylvania**. The t-shirts featured the legendary faceless hooper and different trash talk phrases typically heard on the blacktops across America. ## **AND1: Origins**

In the mid-1990s, AND1 was chugging along as just another basketball brand. That is, until a fateful day in 1998.**A tape was delivered to AND1** containing blurry, homemade streetball footage by a high school basketball coach from Queens, New York. The tape featured a spectacular New York City point guard by the name of [**Rafer Alston, aka Skip To My Lou**](https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/alstora01.html). Having an “aka” was about to get wildly popular. And the videotape would soon be known as the **“Skip Tape”**.
> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/B0TpTWyHB5m/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)  
> [A post shared by RetroRoundball Until Rapture (@thisdayinhoops)](https://www.instagram.com/p/B0TpTWyHB5m/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

> [A post shared by THG (@thehoopgods)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BXRGqNbHOHe/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
Early in 1999, after a failed traditional marketing campaign, AND1 decided to use the “Skip tape” as a marketing tool and reprinted **50,000 copies**. Over the next eight weeks, it was distributed to basketball camps, clinics, and record labels. The tape would become the first basketball mixtape, and quickly made Alston an underground celebrity.

## **AND1: Origins**
In the **summer of 1999**, AND1 created a clever marketing strategy that would prove pivotal to the brand. A free highlight tape was given to everyone who purchased AND1 products. The tape was known [**as the AND1 Mixtape**](https://and1.com/pages/and1-reels?utm_source=organic&utm_medium=weartesters&utm_campaign=thirty-years). Approximately **200,000 tapes were distributed in three weeks**, making this promotion one of the most successful in U.S. retail history.
The **effects of this tape were felt in the NBA** and in the basketball world for over a decade as a generation of players copied and introduced this new school of streetball into the zeitgeist. Dunks and handles became “a must” in the NBA, while FG% and threes were an afterthought. Think of Jamal Crawford, Allen Iverson, Jason “White Chocolate” Williams, T-Mac, KG, Paul Pierce, Marbury, and Larry Hughes, just to name a few.

> [A post shared by NEVER NOT BALLIN‘ (@kickz93)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BzFrOE9jcRj/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/CHwBUo9nDHW/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)  
> [A post shared by Distant Replay (@distant_replay)](https://www.instagram.com/p/CHwBUo9nDHW/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
Even though AND1 had Starbury on the roster, they began to recruit more and more NBA players to wear their products – a major power play to compete with bigger brands such as Nike and adidas. Players like**Latrell Sprewell, Kevin Garnett, Larry Hughes and Jamal Crawford** brought AND1 into the national spotlight. The AND1 logo became one of the most common tattoos in the NBA, as clearly seen below:

## **AND1: Origins**
> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/B9ftT3pHtFY/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)  
> [A post shared by NBA THROWBACK (@notorious_big_bad_boy_)](https://www.instagram.com/p/B9ftT3pHtFY/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/B_U0NhihtLJ/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)  
> [A post shared by Larry Hughes Sr (@thereallhughes)](https://www.instagram.com/p/B_U0NhihtLJ/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
During the 2000 All Star weekend, the brand’s most iconic shoe was featured prominently during the best dunk contest in the history of the NBA. Vince Carter strapped on a pair of the classic red and white AND1 Tai Chi and put on the greatest show the dunk contest has ever witnessed. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-OJMLCF5oK4&ab_channel=ESPN
As the 2001 season rolled around, AND1 was closing in on Nike. In only eight years, they had become the **second-largest basketball brand in the United States.**
The **AND1 Mixtape** became a cultural phenomenon. [**Many streetball players reached legendary status**](https://and1.com/pages/mixtape-legends). They were known around the world exclusively by their nicknames: Hot Sauce, Half Man Half Amazing, AO, Black Widow, the Professor, Escalade, Alimoe, Spyda, The Air Up There, Skip to My Lou, and Main Event. If you lived through that era and didn’t try that Hot Sauce move with the spin and tucking the ball under your shirt, we can’t be friends. Just sayin’.
The soundtracks to the mixtapes were incredible, featuring artists like Snoop Dog, Mobb Deep, CNN, MOP, Method Man, GZA, Common, Talib Kwali, and more.

## **AND1: Origins**
AND1 also created a world streetball tour, which was sort of like a hip-hop Harlem Globetrotters. They then added a reality TV show and even [**released a video game**](https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/and-1-streetball-review/1900-6152598/). The success of AND1 had the basketball shoe market on their heels scrambling to ride the streetball wave.
**EA Sports released the NBA and NFL street video games** series (some of the most fun games ever made, in my opinion). Nike put out their battleground product line and video series, while the NBA released the NBA street, ankle breakers, and dunk DVD series. The born-to-ball DVD was even a thing. It wasn’t the best era for technical basketball, but damn, it was fun.

In the mid-1990s, AND1 was chugging along as just another basketball brand. That is, until a fateful day in 1998.**A tape was delivered to AND1** containing blurry, homemade streetball footage by a high school basketball coach from Queens, New York. The tape featured a spectacular New York City point guard by the name of [**Rafer Alston, aka Skip To My Lou**](https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/alstora01.html). Having an “aka” was about to get wildly popular. And the videotape would soon be known as the **“Skip Tape”**.
> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/B0TpTWyHB5m/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)  
> [A post shared by RetroRoundball Until Rapture (@thisdayinhoops)](https://www.instagram.com/p/B0TpTWyHB5m/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/BXRGqNbHOHe/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)  
> [A post shared by THG (@thehoopgods)](https://www.instagram.com/p/BXRGqNbHOHe/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
Early in 1999, after a failed traditional marketing campaign, AND1 decided to use the “Skip tape” as a marketing tool and reprinted **50,000 copies**. Over the next eight weeks, it was distributed to basketball camps, clinics, and record labels. The tape would become the first basketball mixtape, and quickly made Alston an underground celebrity.

## **AND1: Origins**
In the **summer of 1999**, AND1 created a clever marketing strategy that would prove pivotal to the brand. A free highlight tape was given to everyone who purchased AND1 products. The tape was known [**as the AND1 Mixtape**](https://and1.com/pages/and1-reels?utm_source=organic&utm_medium=weartesters&utm_campaign=thirty-years). Approximately **200,000 tapes were distributed in three weeks**, making this promotion one of the most successful in U.S. retail history.
The **effects of this tape were felt in the NBA** and in the basketball world for over a decade as a generation of players copied and introduced this new school of streetball into the zeitgeist. Dunks and handles became “a must” in the NBA, while FG% and threes were an afterthought. Think of Jamal Crawford, Allen Iverson, Jason “White Chocolate” Williams, T-Mac, KG, Paul Pierce, Marbury, and Larry Hughes, just to name a few.

> [A post shared by Larry Hughes Sr (@thereallhughes)](https://www.instagram.com/p/B_U0NhihtLJ/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
During the 2000 All Star weekend, the brand’s most iconic shoe was featured prominently during the best dunk contest in the history of the NBA. Vince Carter strapped on a pair of the classic red and white AND1 Tai Chi and put on the greatest show the dunk contest has ever witnessed. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-OJMLCF5oK4&ab_channel=ESPN
As the 2001 season rolled around, AND1 was closing in on Nike. In only eight years, they had become the **second-largest basketball brand in the United States.**
The **AND1 Mixtape** became a cultural phenomenon. [**Many streetball players reached legendary status**](https://and1.com/pages/mixtape-legends). They were known around the world exclusively by their nicknames: Hot Sauce, Half Man Half Amazing, AO, Black Widow, the Professor, Escalade, Alimoe, Spyda, The Air Up There, Skip to My Lou, and Main Event. If you lived through that era and didn’t try that Hot Sauce move with the spin and tucking the ball under your shirt, we can’t be friends. Just sayin’.
The soundtracks to the mixtapes were incredible, featuring artists like Snoop Dog, Mobb Deep, CNN, MOP, Method Man, GZA, Common, Talib Kwali, and more.

## **AND1: Origins**
AND1 also created a world streetball tour, which was sort of like a hip-hop Harlem Globetrotters. They then added a reality TV show and even [**released a video game**](https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/and-1-streetball-review/1900-6152598/). The success of AND1 had the basketball shoe market on their heels scrambling to ride the streetball wave.
**EA Sports released the NBA and NFL street video games** series (some of the most fun games ever made, in my opinion). Nike put out their battleground product line and video series, while the NBA released the NBA street, ankle breakers, and dunk DVD series. The born-to-ball DVD was even a thing. It wasn’t the best era for technical basketball, but damn, it was fun.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GI4ilfUnNsw&ab_channel=RyanVanDusen

## 1996 STEPHON MARBURY
In 1996, legendary NBA player and future Hall of Famer Stephon Marbury became AND1’s first NBA ambassador, paving the way for the scores of players the brand would sign in the years to come. Marbury was named to the All-Rookie Team in’97 and went on to lead the Timberwolves to the NBA Playoffs in ‘97 and’98, bringing AND1 much fame in its early stages.
With the Marbury signing, AND1 launched its first pair of basketball sneakers, essentially expanding the brand into the footwear category. The brand debuted its footwear at the 1997 NBA All-Star Game, officially releasing the Stephon Marburys, which wound up becoming one of AND1’s greatest shoes.
![Image 4](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/mixtapes-04.png?v=1784544809&width=1000)
texts.4:
## 1998 THE SKIP TAPE
In late 1998, a videotape containing streetball stunts was delivered to AND1 by a high school coach in New York. The low-quality video was a “mixtape” of hip-hop music and dazzling basketball moves by a streetballer named Rafer Alston, who had just entered the 1998 NBA Draft.
A short while later, AND1 edited and reprinted 50,000 digital copies of Alston’s Mixtape and distributed them across America through basketball camps, clinics and record labels. The tape instantly became the buzz of the basketball world.
The videotape was later known as the "Skip Tape," referring to Alston's streetball nickname "Skip 2 My Lou." Alston, although not yet in the NBA, would soon sign with AND1.
![Image 5](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/mixtapes-05.png?v=1784544901&width=1000)
texts.5:
## 1999 THE MIXTAPE
Once the “Skip Tape” created major buzz for AND1, the brand began to produce multiple “AND1 Mixtapes." [The Mixtapes](https://and1.com/pages/mixtape-legends "Mixtape Legends") were all similar to the Skip Tape - clips of highly entertaining streetball moves with hip-hop and rap playing in the background.
The Mixtape would soon become a major selling tool with the Sports Specialty Retailers. AND1 partnered with FootAction in the summer of ‘99 to start distributing the mixtape nationally, with FootAction offering a free Mixtape DVD with the purchase of any sneakers or apparel. Demand for the tapes reached an unprecedented level as approximately 200,000 tapes were distributed in the span of three weeks, making the Mixtape one of the most successful promotions in US retail history.
The Mixtape’s success resulted in AND1 touring the country every summer in search of the next streetball legends to appear on subsequent Mixtapes.
![Image 6](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/Picture6.jpg?v=1784545028&width=922)
texts.6:
## 2000 THE DUNK CONTEST
The AND1 Tai Chis were always one of the brand’s greatest shoes, known for both performance and style with a yin yang look. But in 2000, they were instantly vaulted into the stratosphere. At the time Vince Carter was between contracts, so he decided to give the Tai Chis a go. Carter then put on one of the greatest performances in NBA Dunk Contest history—all while wearing the red and white Tai Chis.
In the words of Ryan Drew, former VP of footwear at AND1: “Not only was that maybe the best series of dunks I have ever seen, because it was just dunks that you’d never even seen before, but it was almost like the dunks that he had done were tailor made for the color-blocking of the shoe. The dunk where he goes between the legs, he’s got one leg up and the ball is under, and you see one half red and one half white. It was unbelievable. Then, every single image for the next three or four months that was NBA related was him in the Dunk Contest with our shoe on.”
![Image 7](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/marbury2-07.png?v=1784545250&width=1000)
texts.7:
## 2001 NBA AMBASSADORS
Beginning with the Marbury signing and the Rafer Alston discovery two years later, NBA players throughout the league began to sign with AND1, siding with the "underdog" in a major power play competing with the bigger brands. By the 2001 season, AND1 was second in market share among NBA endorsees, just eight years after its inception.
Players like Latrell Sprewell, Kevin Garnett and Jamal Crawford brought AND1 into the national spotlight. The players AND1 signed always matched the brand’s streetball profile, with the in-your-face, best-on-court attitude.
![Image 8](https://and1.com/cdn/shop/files/mixtape_bus-08.png?v=1784545452&width=1000)

[Netflix](https://www.complex.com/tag/netflix) has unleashed the trailer for the latest installment of its _UNTOLD_ sports [documentary](https://www.complex.com/tag/documentary) series,_The Rise and Fall of And1_.
The documentary chronicles how three young friends launched the“And1 Mixtape Tour,” a traveling basketball competition and a corresponding basketball apparel company.The beloved ‘90s brand ultimately crumbled,and the doc examines what led to its rise and eventual downfall.
“To tell the story of And1 you have to tell the story of grit, passion, perseverance and an undying love of the game of basketball,” director Kevin Wilson Jr. said in a statement.“Not only is this the story of streetball legends who kicked off a culture shifting movement and lived out their dreams to get paid to hoop when virtually everyone else shut them out. **AND1** is an American footwear and clothing company specializing in [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") shoes, clothing, and sporting goods. AND1 was founded on August 13, 1993. The company focuses strictly on basketball and is a subsidiary of Galaxy Universal.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-galax-1)
The company sponsors [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA "NBA") athletes, as well as numerous high school and AAU teams in the United States.

In 1993, AND1 began as a graduate school project [partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partnership "Partnership") of Jay Coen Gilbert, Seth Berger, and Tom Austin while they were graduate students at the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania")'s [Wharton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School "Wharton School").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:042-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:1-3) The company name is derived from a phrase used by [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball")[broadcasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_presenter "Sports presenter") to denote a [free throw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_throw "Free throw") awarded to a player against whom a foul has been committed while scoring a goal.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:44-4)

### The Skip Tape and success
Paying homage to Brooklyn streetball culture, AND1 partnered with _[SLAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slam\_(magazine) "Slam (magazine)")_ magazine to host numerous events surrounding the [2015 NBA All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_All-Star_Game "2015 NBA All-Star Game"), played at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [downtown Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Brooklyn "Downtown Brooklyn"). Various charity events with two of New York's greatest streetball legends Lance Stephenson and [Rafer "Skip to My Lou" Alston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafer_Alston "Rafer Alston") were followed by the launch of an exclusive pop-up retail lounge on Flatbush Avenue across from Barclays Center.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-IR222-31)
In July 2016, AND1 signed [Brooklyn Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets "Brooklyn Nets") guard [Sean Kilpatrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Kilpatrick "Sean Kilpatrick").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-32) Over one hundred AND1 High School and AAU teams play across America in various tournaments and leagues, and an AND1 circuit in the making.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-35) In 2017, the brand introduced its own youth basketball circuit under the Dominate the Game name.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-37)

### The Skip Tape and success
Looking to re-establish itself in the market, AND1 announced in 2018 that Kevin Garnett would serve Creative Director and Global Ambassador.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-38) It also named [Jevon Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jevon_Carter "Jevon Carter") and Thomas Beauchamp as ambassadors.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-39) In 2019, AND1 signed [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors") point guard [Fred VanVleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_VanVleet "Fred VanVleet") to a major sponsorship deal and helped introduce the company's Action 2.0 shoe.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-40)[Montrezl Harrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montrezl_Harrell "Montrezl Harrell") also briefly signed on before the deal fell through, though he continued to wear AND1 shoes.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-41) In 2021, the company signed VanVleet's teammate [Norman Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Powell "Norman Powell").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-42)

### The Skip Tape and success
On August 31, 2021, Sequential Brands, AND1's parent, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-43) In September 2021, AND1 was acquired by Galaxy Universal.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-galax-1)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-45) In 2022, AND1 was featured in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") documentary [Untold: The Rise and Fall of And1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Untold:_The_Rise_and_Fall_of_AND1 "Untold: The Rise and Fall of AND1") from director [Kevin Wilson Jr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Wilson_Jr. "Kevin Wilson Jr.").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:042-2)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-46) For its 30th anniversary in 2023, AND1 reintroduced its open run events in order to foster a new generation of streetball.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:62-16)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-47) In 2024, the company released a short documentary on the career of [Ben Wallace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Wallace_(basketball) "Ben Wallace (basketball)").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-49) It also introduced [Alexis Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Morris "Alexis Morris") as its first female ambassador.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-50)

The AND1 team

### The Skip Tape and success
AND1's summer tours began in 1999. The original group included Half Man Half Amazing, Shane the Dribble Machine, [Main Event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waliyy_Dixon "Waliyy Dixon"), Aircraft, [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malloy_Nesmith_Sr. "Malloy Nesmith Sr."), and Headache.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:44-4) In 2002, the tour was expanded into the [AND1 Mixtape Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1_Mixtape_Tour "AND1 Mixtape Tour"), featuring [streetball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streetball "Streetball") players of fame.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-chicago-sports-review3-6) Other standouts were [Skip to My Lou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafer_Alston "Rafer Alston"), [The Professor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grayson_Boucher "Grayson Boucher"), [Hot Sauce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Champion "Philip Champion"), [Spyda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Chism "Dennis Chism"), 50, and [AO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Owens "Aaron Owens").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:2-22)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:7-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-52) From 2002 to 2008, the tours were televised live on ESPN under the name “Streetball”[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:542-11) and competed with ESPN's [SportsCenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SportsCenter "SportsCenter") for the highest ratings.

**AND1** is an American footwear and clothing company specializing in [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") shoes, clothing, and sporting goods. AND1 was founded on August 13, 1993. The company focuses strictly on basketball and is a subsidiary of Galaxy Universal.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-galax-1)
The company sponsors [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA "NBA") athletes, as well as numerous high school and AAU teams in the United States.
texts.1: In 1993, AND1 began as a graduate school project [partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partnership "Partnership") of Jay Coen Gilbert, Seth Berger, and Tom Austin while they were graduate students at the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania")'s [Wharton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School "Wharton School").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:042-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:1-3) The company name is derived from a phrase used by [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball")[broadcasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_presenter "Sports presenter") to denote a [free throw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_throw "Free throw") awarded to a player against whom a foul has been committed while scoring a goal.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AND1#cite_note-:44-4)

Paying homage to Brooklyn streetball culture, AND1 partnered with _[SLAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slam\_(magazine) "Slam (magazine)")_ magazine to host numerous events surrounding the [2015 NBA All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_All-Star_Game "2015 NBA All-Star Game"), played at the [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [downtown Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Brooklyn "Downtown Brooklyn"). ## Netflix has unleashed the trailer for the latest installment of its'UNTOLD'sports documentary series, which chronicles the rise and fall of the“And1 Mixtape
By[Joe Price](https://www.complex.com/author/backwoodsaltar)
July 27, 2022
Comment Save Share ADD COMPLEX ON GOOGLE
Comments
[Netflix](https://www.complex.com/tag/netflix) has unleashed the trailer for the latest installment of its _UNTOLD_ sports [documentary](https://www.complex.com/tag/documentary) series,_The Rise and Fall of And1_.
The documentary chronicles how three young friends launched the“And1 Mixtape Tour,” a traveling basketball competition and a corresponding basketball apparel company.The beloved ‘90s brand ultimately crumbled,and the doc examines what led to its rise and eventual downfall.
“To tell the story of And1 you have to tell the story of grit, passion, perseverance and an undying love of the game of basketball,” director Kevin Wilson Jr. said in a statement.“Not only is this the story of streetball legends who kicked off a culture shifting movement and lived out their dreams to get paid to hoop when virtually everyone else shut them out. It’s also the story of regular people around the world who, because of And1, finally gained access to the energy and pandemonium of in-person high skilled, high energy basketball.”
As Wilson pointed out, the Mixtape Tour brought thrilling basketball games to communities that otherwise couldn’t afford to attend NBA or NCAA games.
“The first time I remember going into an arena to see a game was when And1 came to town. And1 made that arena accessible for ALL of us, not just for the privileged few,” Wilson added.“And1 was fun, gritty streetball FOR THE CULTURE. I’m truly honored to have had the opportunity to chronicle the ascent and ultimate demise of such an iconic moment in sports history. Mac and Chap Way deserve a lot of credit for encouraging us to capture the raw, unfiltered, gritty truth of AND1 straight from the mouths of the Founders and Players who lived the experience.”
